key_insight: A shock-loaded viscoelastic interface can evolve either in oscillatory or monotonic early-time modes, and the transition between them is controlled by a critical viscoelastic number set mainly by density and viscosity contrasts.
engineering_relevance: The analysis offers a theoretical criterion for predicting how soft, shock-loaded materials and fluid/solid interfaces will respond immediately after impact, which is relevant to blast injury modeling and interface design.
method: Linear stability analysis of the early post-shock evolution of a single-mode perturbed interface
Incompressible Cauchy momentum equation coupled with a Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic constitutive model
Derived an implicit dispersion relation for growth rates and examined four representative contrast cases
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical study with analytical dispersion relations and case comparisons, but does not mention experiments or numerical validation data.
watch_item: The result is limited to early-time, linear, incompressible behavior for a single-mode perturbation, so later nonlinear effects and compressibility are not captured.
paper_title: Early-time dynamics of the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability at Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic interfaces
